changes.reason: Add a verified Workers runtime claim for the existing Resend provider, with real workerd HTTP and durable Engagement receipt fixtures. No duplicate provider or domain engine is introduced.

kubernetes.reason: The existing Node provider and SDK are reused without changing transport behavior. No Kubernetes deployment is exercised by this change.
constraints: Existing Node runtime support remains; no live Kubernetes or Resend certification.

aws-lambda.reason: The unchanged provider retains its Lambda runtime claim. This change tests local Workers rather than an AWS invocation.
constraints: Await send and durable receipt writes within the invocation lifetime; no live AWS or Resend certification.

cloudflare.reason: The existing Fetch-based Resend SDK and provider execute in actual local workerd. Separate PostgreSQL fixtures verify durable dispatch, execution and ContactPolicy receipts.
constraints: Requires nodejs_compat and explicit secret binding; provider selection remains optional.
Synthetic Resend HTTP upstream and local PostgreSQL do not verify live Resend, deployed Hyperdrive or full SaaS profile certification.
Complete send and receipt persistence within the callback; no caller deadline or remote cancellation guarantee. Large broadcast requires durable Queue/Task execution.
Provider acceptance is not delivery. Retain committed unknown reservations after ambiguous acceptance; no outer transaction around remote send.

evidence.testName: Resend on actual workerd with a synthetic HTTP upstream sends rendered email using the secret binding and reports provider acceptance
